haiku-low.q1: 401 Unauthorized. The rate-limit store is never touched, so no counter is affected.
haiku-low.q2: Up to the plan limit per minute in total (Standard: 100), because all of a customer's API keys share one counter.
haiku-low.q3: 429 Too Many Requests with Retry-After: N and no X-RateLimit headers. The backend never sees the request; it is not forwarded.
haiku-low.q4: No. Rejected requests do not increment, and the count stays unchanged.
haiku-low.q5: Yes. The count is kept even if the backend failed; a backend failure does not refund it.
haiku-low.q6: It is forwarded anyway (fail open), with metric ratelimit_store_unavailable emitted and no X-RateLimit headers. Up to 50 ms is added first.
haiku-low.q7: Standard: 100 requests per minute. Enterprise: OPEN, not decided by Product, no number chosen.
haiku-low.q8: One shared Redis instance, with one key per customer per window (rl:{customerId}:{windowStart}). Old counts are cleaned up by EXPIRE 120.
haiku-low.q9: NOT STATED. The window is a fixed clock-aligned minute with a new key each window, but the document does not explicitly say budget resets.
haiku-low.q10: Redis runs the atomic script one at a time, so concurrent requests from different gateways cannot both take the last slot.
haiku-low.q11: Seconds left in the window: windowStart + 60 minus Redis time, rounded up, at least 1. Only Redis time is used.
haiku-low.q12: No retry, local counter, or circuit breaker in v1. The client gets no X-RateLimit headers on a fail-open response.

sonnet.q1: It gets a 401 Unauthorized. No rate-limit counter is touched (Redis is never called).
sonnet.q2: They share one counter, so the total across all keys is limited to the customer's plan limit per minute (Standard = 100; Enterprise undecided). Keys do not get separate budgets.
sonnet.q3: A 429 Too Many Requests with a Retry-After: N header (no X-RateLimit headers). The backend never sees the request; it is not forwarded.
sonnet.q4: No. Rejected requests do not increment the count, and no budget is used.
sonnet.q5: Yes. The count is incremented at check time and is kept even if the backend fails (no refund).
sonnet.q6: The gateway fails open: it emits the metric ratelimit_store_unavailable and forwards the request to the backend, returning the response without X-RateLimit headers.
sonnet.q7: Standard = 100 requests per minute. Enterprise is OPEN: Product has not decided, no number chosen.
sonnet.q8: In one shared Redis instance (with a replica for failover), in a key per customer per window: rl:{customerId}:{windowStart}. The key's EXPIRE 120 removes old counters (cleanup only).
sonnet.q9: When the fixed one-minute, clock-aligned window (based on Redis time) rolls over, a new key starts at 0 for the new windowStart.
sonnet.q10: The check-and-increment is a single atomic Redis script. Redis runs scripts one at a time, so concurrent requests from different gateways cannot both take the last slot.
sonnet.q11: Using Redis time only: the seconds left in the current window (windowStart + 60 - time), rounded up, with a minimum of 1. Gateway clocks are not used.
sonnet.q12: No. There is no retry, local counter or circuit breaker in v1. The client gets neither X-RateLimit-Limit nor X-RateLimit-Remaining (no rate-limit headers), because the values are unknown.
